findings.statement: 16 MB seals lift ingest-to-routed by at least 1.2x over 64 MB
findings.detail: 16 MB 437390 ops/s against 64 MB 439112 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.996, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB 452531 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.031, p=0.2101) -- within noise, not a result). Phases at 16 against 64 MB: commit 0.012s/0.014s, seal 0.012s/0.013s, merge 0.012s/0.011s; the loop alone 0.021s/0.024s. Smaller seals move the merges off the drain and onto the other cores while the load runs

findings.statement: at 16 MB seals, device bytes are at most 2.0x the 64 MB arm's
findings.detail: device bytes 10.0 MB at 16 MB seals against 10.0 at 64 MB (1.000x); 32 MB 10.0, 8 MB 10.0. Disk after the drain 3.7/3.7/3.7/3.7 MB for 64/32/16/8, partitions 1/1/1/1. Every merge round rewrites the live set the new pieces touch; this is that amplification, measured

findings.statement: reads after the drain do not differ across seal sizes
findings.detail: 166 ns per point read at 64 MB, 152 at 32, 163 at 16 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.989, p=0.4712) -- within noise, not a result), 172 at 8 (8mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.037, p=0.8102) -- within noise, not a result). After the drain every arm is partitions only and the partition count is set by max_keys, not the seal size

findings.statement: the sweep has an interior optimum: 8 MB seals ingest no faster than 16 MB
findings.detail: 8 MB 449173 ops/s against 16 MB 437390 (8mb vs 16mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.027, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result); device bytes 10.0 against 10.0 MB, merge phase 0.011s against 0.012s.
